model.name: Storage/identity RE-KEY — key data/users/ by a non-secret opaque storageId (never accepted for auth) so a credential rotation touches ONLY auth + ZERO path bytes (no orphaned home)
model.description: SECURITY (design landed 03287719c, fresh expert builds after the 116 invalidation): the owner token is BOTH the auth credential AND the storage key (it appears in data/users/<token>/ paths), so rotating it orphans the user's home — measured to have threatened TRON's. And there are 217 distinct such credentials, not one. FIX = re-key storage onto a purpose-built OPAQUE storageId (non-secret, minted per owner, appears in paths, NEVER accepted for auth) BEFORE any rotation, so afterwards a token rotation changes only auth and touches zero path bytes. Bridge (storage dual-validity) during the migration, kill mint-regrowth at the three sites, gate that no path carries a credential-shaped segment. Ties R40.21 (capability-not-identity) + R40.14/R40.15. NO credential VALUE recorded here (secret-value rule); owner referenced only as <owner-id>/<token>.

discoverySource.note: Requirement-grade security finding, capture-only for Tron's backlog. Exploit/rotation detail lives in the LOCAL design (/var/dev/security-local/, chmod 600) — NOT in-repo. Independent of tonight's incident; architect design/verdict fills the shape. NO exploitable detail + NO secret VALUES in this unit (secret-value rule).

acceptanceCriteria.text: A purpose-built OPAQUE storageId keys data/users/ — non-secret, minted per owner, may appear in paths, and is NEVER accepted for auth. ★ LOAD-BEARING: because it cannot authenticate, leaking it in a path is HARMLESS -> credential/path re-conflation is STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE, not merely fixed. NOT the Profile uuid (architect measured 0/195 Devices + 0/45 Rooms resolve to a Profile on disk = no universal stable owner-id; token->profile is runtime-only).

BRIDGE, not a hard-rename, during transition: BOTH the old-token path AND the new-storageId path resolve, then converge, then the old drops = STORAGE dual-validity. Makes the migration RECOVERABLE, not atomic-or-broken.

Migration treatment: dry-run WITH counts first; rewrite the 167 unitLinks; per-file content-hash before==after (zero content loss); idempotent (re-run = no-op); half-run-recoverable. Same remap rigor as R27.2.

Kill mint-regrowth at ALL THREE sites — anchored by SYMBOL (line numbers DRIFT: the 2 server calls already moved +2 to 1998/2011 after an authz re-point above them; anchor on the symbol, never the line): (1) createUserHome (UserKeys.ts), (2) roomFsLink (file-unit.ts), (3) the server upload mint = createWebItemUnit + createFileUnit (server.ts, 2 calls) — or the migration REFILLS behind us with fresh token-keyed homes.

★ THE GATE (ci:gates, beside the field pii-guard): NO token-keyed path remains AND NO path string contains a credential-shaped segment; every unitLink resolves; per-file hashes match; idempotent. STUB-MUST-FAIL BOTH ways (plant a credential-shaped path segment -> RED; weaken the guard -> RED).

★★ THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION THAT PROTECTS TRON: storage is keyed by storageId BEFORE any rotation, and AFTER the re-key a token rotation changes ONLY auth and touches ZERO path/file bytes — PROVEN by a post-re-key rotation test (rotate a token -> assert 0 path bytes changed, home still resolves).

SEQUENCING: the 116-invalidation (auth-only, touches no storage) runs FIRST; the FRESH expert builds this gated re-key migration AFTER it, with the architect backstopping. Design landed (03287719c) — no longer design-blocked, but gated on the migration ACs above.

supersededACs.text: The user-id (identity primary key) stays STABLE across credential rotation — no migration of device enrollments / memberships / ownership refs on a rotate.
A SEPARATE, ROTATABLE credential (distinct from the user-id) authenticates; rotating it does NOT touch identity.
Rotation causes NO lockout (owner still authenticates) and NO orphaned refs (every identity ref still resolves to the stable user-id).
The credential mechanism is challenge-response / keypair (not a shared secret at rest) — ties R40.14 (loginToken keypair) + R40.15 (secretCode hardening) + R40.21 (capability tokens).
★ DESIGN-REQUIRED: the architect's measurement/verdict fills the shape and may reshape the rotation. Do NOT build before the verdict.

model.premiseAmendment: ★ PREMISE MEASURED FALSE, TWICE (honest amendment, not a quiet replace — see supersededACs): the original R40.22 was written as SINGLE-OWNER credential/identity decoupling (rotate ONE owner secret, dual-validity, flip a flag). Measurement destroyed that premise: (1) there are 217 DISTINCT credentials tracked (ownerToken 241 + uploaderToken 204 etc), not one owner secret; (2) the token is ALSO the user's STORAGE KEY — it appears in data/users/<token>/ paths, so rotating it ORPHANS the home (it would have orphaned TRON's). So R40.22's real scope is a STORAGE/IDENTITY RE-KEY, and its ACs must say so or we build to a spec the data contradicts. Amended per architect design 03287719c + PO ruling 2026-08-11; original ACs preserved in supersededACs. This credential incident IS R40.22's live justification.
